key_insight: Y6 excitons are mixed Frenkel–charge-transfer states with 20–40% charge-transfer character, enabling delocalization-mediated transport and rapid interfacial quenching.
engineering_relevance: These results provide a quantitative basis for designing single-component organic solar cells with improved charge separation by tuning molecular coupling, film morphology, and interface energetics.
method: Ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy on Y6 films interfaced with hole-transport layers
Analytical hybrid Frenkel–charge-transfer model to fit quenching dynamics
Extraction of electronic coupling, charge-transfer fraction, and system-bath interaction strength
evidence_signal: Experimental analysis of the transient absorption data shows ~1 ps exciton quenching within ~4 nm of the interface, supporting a short-range injection mechanism.
watch_item: The model is fitted to a specific Y6/interlayer system, so transferring the parameters or conclusions to other non-fullerene acceptors may require revalidation.
paper_title: Quantitative Analysis of Exciton Composition and Dynamics in Y6 Films for Single-Component Solar Cells
